title: Per-model 'grace gates' for dependency isolation and safe fallback orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: A single overloaded dependency (model shard, third-party reranker, or multi-tenant GPU pool) can cause cascading latency spikes and request failures. Existing coarse circuit breakers either flip too aggressively (causing user-visible quality regressions) or too late (causing SLO violations).

Goal: Implement a per-dependency and per-model isolation primitive ("grace gate") that trips predictably based on multi-signal thresholds, provides tunable soft/veto behavior, and orchestrates safe fallback flows (local model variant, cached response, degraded mode) with measurable health signals to the Console and SLO engine. The system should support inheritance from global policies and tenant-level overrides, and expose controls for canary rollouts and emergency manual override.
acceptance_criteria: Grace gate can be configured per-model, per-dependency, and per-tenant via service config and UI
Trip decisions use at least 3 signals (error rate, p95 latency, and backend CPU saturation) and implement hysteresis to avoid flapping
Fallback orchestration supports ordered strategies: cached-prefix -> cheaper-quantized-variant -> async-degrade-with-token -> hard-fail, with observable execution counts
Rollout plan for experiment on two non-critical models with canary (10% traffic) and automatic rollback on SLO regression
Metrics emitted: grace_gate_state, trip_reason, trip_window_evaluation, fallback_taken (all tagged by model, tenant, region)
Unit + integration tests cover trip window edge cases and fallback fall-through behavior
Documentation and Console controls for overrides and policy templates are published
implementation_steps: Add grace_gate controller to routing layer with pluggable signal evaluators
Implement signal collectors (latency histogram EWMA, error-count sliding-window, host/cpu headroom)
Define policy inheritance and normalization for per-tenant overrides
Instrument fallback executor and expose counters to metrics infra
Integrate with SLO engine to report budget burn and enable automated canary rollback
Ship UI controls in Console: policy editor, real-time gate state, emergency bypass
Create chaos-test harness to rehearse multi-region failover with grace gates enabled
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We favor multi-signal evaluation (error+latency+resource) rather than pure error-rate to reduce false trips during cold-start spikes
Hysteresis window chosen: 60s evaluation + 3 consecutive windows to trip, 5 consecutive windows to heal (configurable) to reduce oscillation
Fallback ordering prioritizes user-perceived content fidelity (cache first) before cheaper quantized variants to preserve quality
We will first implement gate logic in the routing plane (low-latency) with eventual move to a shared policy engine if cross-service reuse becomes necessary
Manual override will be gated by RBAC and audit-logged to satisfy Private deployment requirements
risks: Incorrect thresholds could result in large-scale quality regressions if fallback selection is too aggressive
Adding evaluators to the hot path increases complexity and slight CPU overhead on routing hosts
Policy inheritance mistakes could leave tenants with overly permissive or overly strict defaults
mitigations: Start with conservative defaults and run canaries at 10% traffic with realtime SLO monitors before broader rollout
Benchmark routing-plane evaluator overhead under p99 load; optimize via sampling and offload heavy analyzers to sidecar when necessary
Add config linting and unit tests for inheritance rules; provide tenant-safe sandbox mode
